title: Jalal al-Din Rumi — Masnavi-yi Ma'navi, the Six Books, in Persian (Ganjoor)
edition: Masnavi, Book One (دفتر اول); Masnavi, Book Two (دفتر دوم); Masnavi, Book Three (دفتر سوم); Masnavi, Book Four (دفتر چهارم); Masnavi, Book Five (دفتر پنجم); Masnavi, Book Six (دفتر ششم)

license.payload: Public domain: Rumi d. 1273. The transcription is Ganjoor's (ganjoor.net), which names its source for each section and states of its texts: 'هم‌اکنون منبع عمدهٔ آثار موجود در این مجموعه منابع آزاد در دسترس همگان است' (the principal source of the works in this collection is free sources available to all), releasing them on the principle 'دگران کاشتند و ما خوردیم، ما بکاریم و دیگران بخورند' (others planted and we ate; we plant and others will eat). Ganjoor's statement is recorded as given; it is not a formal licence.

normalization: Project Gutenberg texts stripped at the START/END markers, CRLF to LF, otherwise unaltered; Internet Archive OCR text layers as fetched, uncorrected (text/<slug>.ocr.txt) — the scan under original/<identifier>/ is the witness; Ganjoor JSON as fetched, rendered one couplet per line, hemistichs joined by ' / ', section titles marked '=== title ==='.
scope: The Masnavi entire, all six books, in Persian, one text per book. Ganjoor's prose summaries of couplets and its recitations are not seated. The printed edition behind the transcription is not stated in the fetched data beyond Ganjoor's per-section source name, which is recorded. Nicholson's critical edition (Leiden: Brill, 1925–1933) and his translation are not seated: original language only, by ruling. Whinfield's abridged English (1887; 1898) is public domain and not seated for the same reason. The Divan-e Shams-e Tabrizi is not seated in this pass: QUEUED.
verified_loci: Book One, section 1 (سرآغاز), the first couplet: 'بشنو این نی چون شکایت می‌کند / از جدایی‌ها حکایت می‌کند' — the Song of the Reed
why_seated: Rumi asked for by name, in the original. The Masnavi opens with the reed cut from its bed and telling the story of its separation: transmission out of loss, the archive's oldest subject, from the other side of the medieval world.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-10-18: "did we ever seat the medieval pearl poem in the originals library?" — "rumi, too - and gibran's the prophet if its public domain" — "and blake" — "yes, original language where available always, the prophet full, and lets do illuminated books as text to start. we can group those all in a single ea-corpora deposit, refer to examples, and they also do to alexanarch data and get spines and cards on traininglayerliterature's originals library".
